title: Post-Utility Life Design
opening: Some commitments can start to feel like proof that you deserve your place. Test a modest change in one area before drawing a conclusion about your whole life.

example.title: One optional task
example.body: A person stops volunteering for one future optional task while keeping current promises or renegotiating any change that affects someone else. They notice the practical effects and what the time serves. If the task is a real responsibility, they redesign the trial.

labels.areaPrompt: Where does performance feel tied to your worth? Name one recurring situation; you do not need to explain more than you want to.
labels.changePrompt: What could you change for a short trial, without breaking a promise?
labels.commitments: Keep people and promises in view
labels.commitmentsPrompt: What needs to stay covered, or who would need to agree to a change? You can leave this blank if no one else is affected.
labels.reviewWindow: The manuscript suggests two weeks. Use that window when it fits; choose another period, review after one attempt, or skip a timed trial if it would create risk or burden.
labels.reviewPrompt: What changed in daily life? How did the trial feel? Record a benefit, a neutral result, or a problem, even if it differs from what you expected.
labels.decisionPrompt: Keep, revise, or stop the change? If it caused a real cost or left a responsibility uncovered, what will you repair or renegotiate?
